title: Telling when a cake is done, and why it went wrong

items.stem: You insert a toothpick into the center of a cake and pull it out. Which result means the cake is done?

options.text: It comes out covered in wet batter
It comes out clean or with dry crumbs
It comes out with a thin layer of flour stuck to it
It comes out clean, but the center feels cool

items.stem: Besides the toothpick test, name one other sign that tells you a cake is done.
A cake looks fully baked, but the middle sinks as it cools even though the toothpick test was clean and it baked the full time. What's the most likely cause?

options.text: It was left in the oven too long
The batter was overmixed before baking
Too much leavener was used in it
The batter sat out too long before baking

items.stem: A cake comes out of the oven with a tall, cracked dome instead of a flat top. What most likely caused this?

options.text: The oven ran too hot while it baked
The cake pan was greased too heavily
The cake was pulled out before it finished
The batter was mixed for too short a time

items.stem: A cake tastes dry and crumbly even though you measured every ingredient correctly. What's a likely cause involving the oven or baking time?
You cut into a cake and the middle is wetter than the edges, though a toothpick near the edge came out clean. What does this most likely mean?

options.text: The cake needs more sugar in the batter
The edges of the cake were overbaked
The pan should be greased more heavily
The toothpick missed the slower-baking middle
